# 1 Kings Chapter 15 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** In the eighteenth year of King Jeroboam son of Nebat, Abijam became king of Judah.

**2** He reigned three years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Maacah daughter of Abishalom.

**3** He committed all the same sins his father had committed before him. His heart was not fully devoted to the LORD his God, as David his ancestor's heart had been.

**4** But for David's sake, the LORD his God kept a lamp burning for him in Jerusalem by raising up a son to succeed him and by keeping Jerusalem secure.

**5** David had done what was right in the LORD's eyes and had never failed to obey any of the LORD's commands throughout his life — except in the incident involving Uriah the Hittite.

**6** There was war between Rehoboam and Jeroboam throughout Abijam's life.

**7** The rest of Abijam's reign and everything he did are recorded in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah. There was war between Abijam and Jeroboam.

**8** Abijam died and was buried in the City of David. His son Asa succeeded him as king.

**9** In the twentieth year of King Jeroboam of Israel, Asa became king of Judah.

**10** He reigned forty-one years in Jerusalem. His grandmother's name was Maacah daughter of Abishalom.

**11** Asa did what was right in the LORD's eyes, just as his ancestor David had done.

**12** He expelled the male cult prostitutes from the land and got rid of all the idols his ancestors had made.

**13** He even removed his grandmother Maacah from her position as queen mother because she had made an obscene Asherah pole. Asa cut the thing down and burned it in the Kidron Valley.

**14** The hilltop shrines were not removed, but Asa's heart was fully committed to the LORD throughout his life.

**15** He brought into the LORD's temple the silver, gold, and other items that he and his father had dedicated.

**16** Asa and King Baasha of Israel were at war throughout their reigns.

**17** Baasha king of Israel invaded Judah and fortified Ramah to cut off all traffic to and from King Asa of Judah.

**18** So Asa took all the silver and gold left in the treasuries of the LORD's temple and the royal palace and gave them to his officials. He sent them to Ben-hadad son of Tabrimmon, son of Hezion, king of Aram, who ruled in Damascus, with this message:

**19** "Let's make a treaty, you and I, like the one between our fathers. Here — I'm sending you a gift of silver and gold. Break your treaty with King Baasha of Israel so he'll pull back from me."

**20** Ben-hadad agreed and sent his army commanders against the towns of Israel. They conquered Ijon, Dan, Abel-beth-maacah, and all the region of Chinneroth, along with the whole territory of Naphtali.

**21** When Baasha heard about it, he abandoned the construction at Ramah and withdrew to Tirzah.

**22** Then King Asa issued an order to all Judah — no one was exempt — and they hauled away the stones and timber Baasha had been using at Ramah. King Asa used them to build up Geba in Benjamin and Mizpah.

**23** The rest of Asa's reign — his achievements, his power, and the cities he built — is all recorded in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah. In his old age, however, his feet became diseased.

**24** Asa died and was buried with his ancestors in the City of David. His son Jehoshaphat succeeded him.

**25** Nadab son of Jeroboam became king of Israel in the second year of King Asa of Judah. He ruled Israel for two years.

**26** He did evil in the LORD's sight, following in his father's footsteps and committing the same sin his father had caused Israel to commit.

**27** Baasha son of Ahijah, from the tribe of Issachar, plotted against him and assassinated him at Gibbethon, a Philistine town, while Nadab and all Israel were besieging it.

**28** Baasha killed Nadab in the third year of King Asa of Judah and took the throne.

**29** As soon as he became king, he slaughtered Jeroboam's entire family. He did not leave a single survivor — he wiped them all out, just as the LORD had said through his servant Ahijah of Shiloh.

**30** This happened because of the sins Jeroboam had committed and had caused Israel to commit, and because of how he had provoked the LORD, the God of Israel.

**31** The rest of Nadab's reign and everything he did are recorded in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel.

**32** Asa and Baasha king of Israel were at war throughout their reigns.

**33** In the third year of King Asa of Judah, Baasha son of Ahijah became king over all Israel in Tirzah. He reigned twenty-four years.

**34** He did evil in the LORD's sight, following in the footsteps of Jeroboam and committing the same sin Jeroboam had caused Israel to commit.

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

1. **15:4 — "kept a lamp burning"**: David's lamp — the fragile, persistent metaphor for dynastic continuity. Bad kings come and go, but the lamp survives because of David's merit, not theirs.
2. **15:5 — "except in the incident involving Uriah"**: The narrator's honest footnote. David was righteous — except for the worst thing he ever did. This single clause prevents the Bible from becoming propaganda.
3. **15:13 — reforming his own family**: Asa fires his grandmother. The text doesn't flinch from the personal cost of religious reform. Faithfulness to God sometimes means confronting the people closest to you.
4. **15:29 — the end of a dynasty**: Jeroboam's entire line exterminated, as prophesied. The speed of the report (one verse) matches the speed of the execution. No drama, no mourning — just fulfillment.

— PNEUMA
